title: Review C-D (T-0049): spec_review role, prompt, verdict capture
spec: Adversarial review of commit 41df1ae on task/T-0049 (your worktree is based on that branch; verify `grep spec_review orchestrator/spawn.py` first). Focus: (1) run_worker's spec_review branch reads inputs[0] as a task id and tolerates a missing or non-string input without crashing the worker; (2) code excerpts: scope globs resolved against the right base (reviewed task's goal branch worktree or ROOT), capped at 12,000 chars, never read outside the repo, never follow symlinks out; (3) the verdict write lands on both the spec_review task and the execute task and does not overwrite an existing review_verdict; (4) the prompt template stays under 3,000 chars and asks for JSON only; (5) bus.ROLES.add at import time is a documented temporary hack and nothing else depends on import order; (6) tests use FakeProc, no real subprocess. Run `uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` and report the result line. Return ONLY {"verdict":"approve|request_changes","comments":[...]} under 3,000 chars.

comments.issue: fit_result only shrinks the 'findings' key. spec_review's result carries 'risks' (see spawn.py:223 and spec-review.md's return schema), so an oversize risks list is never truncated. That either leaves the posted result above the 3,000-char acceptance cap, or — once it exceeds bus.MAX_RESULT_CHARS (6000) — makes bus.post() raise ValueError, which the outer try/except then turns into status=failed with no verdict captured at all. Add a 'risks' branch to fit_result (mirroring the findings binary-search trim) and lower the effective cap for this role to 3,000 as specced.

Acceptance requires 'verdict with line-anchored comments', but the schema returns risks as {path, issue, severity} with no line number, and code_excerpts() (spawn.py:242-255) strips original line numbers before building the prompt (splitlines()[:120] joined with no numbering). The reviewing model has no way to anchor an issue to a line, and the schema has nowhere to put one even if it could. Compare to review.md's existing comments schema, which does carry {path, line, issue, severity} — spec-review.md should match it.

Acceptance requires 'test result line reported' but nothing in the spec_review path (prompt, schema, or run_worker's spec_review branch) references test output. Spec review runs before code exists so there's nothing to test yet — if that's the intended reading, the acceptance criterion is stale/mismatched for this task and should be corrected rather than silently left unimplemented.
